facts.statement: A ten-centimetre-long pterosaur fossil was discovered in 1993 by Jean-Jacques Lepage on the Normandy coast near Ecqueville.
facts.quote: In 1993, Jean-Jacques Lepage on the Normandy coast at the Cap de la Hève, near Ecqueville, Octeville-sur-Mer, Seine-Maritime, Normandy, found a ten centimetres long fossil of a pterosaur in a marine claystone layer.

facts.statement: Eric Buffetaut and colleagues named the genus Normannognathus with the type species N. wellnhoferi in 1998.
facts.quote: In 1998, Eric Buffetaut et al. named a separate genus for it. The type species is Normannognathus wellnhoferi.

facts.statement: The snout of Normannognathus is low, pointed, and curves upward.
facts.quote: The snout is low and pointed, and curves upward.

facts.statement: A very tall bony crest abruptly juts out from the premaxillae, forming a crested wave with a concave leading margin.
facts.quote: On the back top of this part a very tall bony crest is present. It abruptly juts out from the premaxillae, formed like a crested wave, having a concave leading margin.

facts.statement: The crest is flat along the midline of the upper jaw and has a fibrous texture that may indicate a horn sheath covering.
facts.quote: The crest is flat, running down the midline of the upper jaw and shows a fibrous texture that could be indicative of some covering, such as a horn sheath.

facts.statement: The teeth are robust, not very elongated, and extend to the very tip of the jaws.
facts.quote: The teeth are robust, and not very elongated. They continue to be present until the very tip of the jaws.

facts.statement: The tooth count is five per premaxilla, at least nine per maxilla, and at least fourteen per dentary.
facts.quote: The tooth count is five per premaxilla; the number is at least nine for the maxilla, and at least fourteen per dentary

facts.statement: Normannognathus lived during the Kimmeridgian age of the Upper Jurassic in the Argiles d'Octeville Formation of France.
facts.quote: Normannognathus is a genus of pterosaur from the Kimmeridgian-age Upper Jurassic Argiles d'Octeville Formation of France.

facts.statement: Normannognathus lived between 152.21 and 149.2 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (152.21 to 149.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Normannognathus was initially classified in the family Germanodactylidae but recent analyses have placed it in various phylogenetic positions.
facts.quote: Initially, Normannognathus was classified to the family Germanodactylidae, sister taxon to Germanodactylus, however, many recent analysis have recovered Normannognathus in different phylogenetic positions

facts.statement: The original classification assigned Normannognathus to the family Germanodactylidae.
The genus is based on a holotype comprising the left front portion of a skull and associated but unarticulated lower jaws.
facts.quote: El género está basado en el holotipo Musée Géologique Cantonal de Lausanne 59'583, la parte frontal izquierda de un cráneo y la mandíbula inferior, hallada asociada a éste pero no articulada.

facts.statement: David Unwin considered Normannognathus to be a basal member of the Dsungaripteroidea in 2006.
facts.quote: David Unwin in 2006 considered it a basal member of the Dsungaripteroidea.

facts.statement: Witton et al. concluded in 2015 that Normannognathus is an indeterminate monofenestratan, sharing characters with both ctenochasmatoids and non-pterodactyloid monofenestratans.
facts.quote: In 2015 however, Witton et al. concluded that it is an indeterminate monofenestratan, noting that it shares some characters with ctenochasmatoids, yet shares other characters with non-pterodactyloid monofenestratans.

rejected.statement: The genus is based on a holotype consisting of the left front portion of a skull and associated but unarticulated lower jaws.
rejected.quote: The genus is based on holotype Musée Géologique Cantonal de Lausanne 59'583, the left front portion of a skull and the associated, but not articulated to it, lower jaws.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the left front portion of a skull and'

rejected.statement: In 2018, Longrich et al. classified Normannognathus as the sister taxon of Cycnorhamphus within the family Gallodactylidae.
rejected.quote: In 2018 however, Longrich et al. found Normannognathus to be the sister taxon of Cycnorhamphus within the family Gallodactylidae, which in turn was within the Ctenochasmatoidea.
